title: The Khalsa Debates How to Strike at the Ravi Crossing

blocks.text: At the river the Sikh chiefs debate the best moment to finish the campaign. Some Singhs opined to let half of Abdali's forces cross the river so that the enemy might then be trapped and plundered in a more decisive blow.

Others urge immediate attack. S. Charat Singh begged the Khalsa to take on Abdali directly, but senior judgment still weighs whether patience might yield a cleaner victory and reminds the assembly that no hasty action was in their interest.

Even so, pressure mounts as Abdali's troops were crossing the river Ravi. The page follows the confusion of attack and withdrawal before the Afghans, badly shaken and eager to escape further punishment, hurry westward and hastily did they march in the direction of Multan.
